clue.text: His aim is to foil his opponent

definitions.text: His aim is to foil his opponent

parts.words: His aim is to foil his opponent
parts.note: reads as someone thwarting a rival, but a foil is also the light sword used in a sporting bout

explanation.walkthrough: 'Foil' looks like a verb meaning thwart; it is also the light blade used in the sport of swordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencing competitor aims to land hits with the foil, a thrusting sword, on an opponent.

clue.text: Paintings found in recess of new building

indicators.note: a new building is something put together afresh, so these letters are reassembled in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Murals discovered in an alcove of a newly built structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new building' signals the anagram: RECESS plus OF rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Frescoes are wall paintings done on wet plaster.

clue.text: One centrally placed in church passage has links with simple attitudes

indicators.note: something placed centrally in a word sits inside it, so one piece goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: the nave is the central passage or body of a church
the Roman numeral one is I
ties are links or bonds

explanation.surface: Someone standing in the middle of a church aisle is linked to unsophisticated views.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is an innocent, unworldly simplicity of outlook; the plural covers such attitudes.

clue.text: Goes off with self-interested people

indicators.note: something gone off has gone wrong, so the letters of the word beside it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Leaves in the company of selfish types.
explanation.definitionFit: Egos stands, by extension, for people driven by self-regard and vanity.

clue.text: Has a bad effect on the Italian fellows' comeback: there's a book about them

indicators.note: a book about them surrounds them, so the book's letters go round the turned pieces

parts.note: Acts is a book of the New Testament

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the Italian article and the fellows are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: il is Italian for the
F is the abbreviation for fellow, so FF stands for fellows

explanation.surface: Italian men making a return are hit hard, and someone has written about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback' turns the Italian article and the fellows together, and 'about them' sends the book round that turned run; 'the Italian fellows' reads like a group of men.
explanation.definitionFit: To afflict is to trouble or harm something, to cause it suffering.

clue.text: Hazel is about to be a terrible flirt

indicators.note: terrible means badly done, so the letters of the words beside it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman called Hazel is about to become a shameless coquette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazel' looks like a woman's name; it is the nut tree. 'terrible' rearranges BE FLIRT.
explanation.definitionFit: A filbert is the cultivated hazel, a tree grown for its edible nuts.

clue.text: Features elegies about one born in France

indicators.note: about means around, so the elegies wrap round the other pieces

parts.note: laments are mournful poems or songs, as elegies are
the Roman numeral one is I
née is French for born, used of a woman's maiden name; written NE here

explanation.surface: Mournful poems written about a French-born person are given prominence.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineaments are the distinctive outlines of a face or body, its characteristic marks.

clue.text: Dog caught soldier carrying the gold

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
or is gold in heraldry
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A dog was caught by a soldier who had the gold on him.
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a small short-legged Welsh breed of dog.

clue.text: Looking out for an agent in Germany

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
taken as written
G is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Watching for a secret operative based in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying on or for something means keeping watch, watching closely to catch sight of it.

clue.text: Headlight of new coach I'm boarding

parts.note: I'm gives its letters without the apostrophe
a bus is a coach

explanation.surface: A traveller climbs aboard a new coach and notices its headlamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headlight' looks like a lamp; it is a halo, light round the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A nimbus is a halo, the luminous disc shown round a saint's head in paintings.

clue.text: Newspaper column turned the tide of speech about one

indicators.note: turned means reshaped, so the letters of the word beside it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: oral means spoken, relating to speech
the Roman numeral one is I

explanation.surface: An opinion piece reversed the trend in public speaking concerning one person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned the tide' looks idiomatic; 'turned' rearranges TIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An editorial is the article stating a newspaper's own opinion, a leader.

clue.text: In New York, Queen Victoria originally seemed apprehensive

indicators.note: in means one piece sits within the other

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter of the following name is used

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria seemed nervous on a visit to New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervy in British usage means jumpy or anxious, uneasy.

clue.text: Took one away from the principal cook

indicators.note: took signals removal: one letter is taken from the following word
away from completes the removal signal, naming the word that loses a letter

parts.note: a chief is the principal or head
the Roman numeral one is I

explanation.surface: Someone removed one item from the head cook's kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional cook, especially the one in charge of a kitchen.

clue.text: Denial that a sailor, for example, is in the race

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: is in means one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a nation is a people or race

explanation.surface: A sailor, perhaps, refusing to join in the race.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnegation is self-denial, the renouncing or rejecting of something.

clue.text: Othello, perhaps, when a bachelor, might have need of space to grow up?

parts.note: to lack something is to need or be without it
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, growing up means the word climbs, read from bottom to top

parts.note: room is space

explanation.surface: Asks whether a young unmarried Othello needed more room to develop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to grow up' climbs the word for space in this down clue. The A of 'a bachelor' is used as well, placed after the need; Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Othello is a Moor; the dated word for a dark-skinned man is used of him.

clue.text: Stay back for the French eats

indicators.note: back means backwards, so the word for stay is read in reverse

parts.note: to bide is to stay or wait
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: Remain behind to get French food.
explanation.definitionFit: Edibles are things fit to eat, food, as eats is informal for food.

clue.text: First mistake in these convoluted subjects

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other
convoluted means twisted, so the letters of the word beside it are rearranged
first means the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: The opening error in these tangled topics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convoluted' makes THEES from THESE; the M of 'mistake' goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Themes are topics or subjects of discussion or of a work.

clue.text: Edward I took up weapons to capture ship intended for a special purpose

indicators.note: I as a regnal numeral means the first, so Edward's first letter is taken
capturing means holding something inside, so the ship goes into the other piece

parts.note: armed means equipped with or took up weapons
an ark is a ship, as Noah's

explanation.surface: King Edward the First armed himself and seized a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edward I' looks like the king; 'I', the first, takes the first letter of Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Earmarked means set aside or reserved for a particular use.

clue.text: Person given right to put his name down in a bishop's domain

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a see is the diocese or seat of a bishop
to sign is to write one's name

explanation.surface: Someone is entitled to put a signature on a register in a diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: An assignee is someone to whom a right or property is transferred in law.

clue.text: The soul of the god's beloved

definitions.meaning: in myth, the mortal girl loved by Cupid (Eros)

explanation.definitionFit: Psyche means the soul or mind, and is the girl Cupid loved in classical myth.

clue.text: Passes first exam, then gives up

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: lapses means lets slip or gives up, falls away

explanation.surface: A student gets through the first test, then drops out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passes' looks like exam success; it is time going by.
explanation.definitionFit: Time elapses when it passes or slips by.

clue.text: Confines sinner to reform him? About time!

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the other piece
to reform is to remake, so the letters of the word beside it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer is locked up in the hope he will change: and not before time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' rearranges SINNER, and 'About' puts it round T.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern is to confine or imprison someone, typically in wartime.

clue.text: Plants former partner in Corsica and Martinique, say

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: both are French islands, and île is French for island
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: An ex-partner is living in Corsica or Martinique.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilex is the holly genus, so the plural names such plants.

clue.text: Tragedy allowed poor actor to be put first

indicators.note: the poor actor is placed before the word for allowed

parts.note: a ham is a bad, overacting actor
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A bad performer was allowed to take the lead in a tragic play.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is one of Shakespeare's best-known tragedies.

clue.text: Annoyed that working garage has to absorb tax on prime diesel

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the tax goes inside the rearranged letters
working means in operation, so the letters of the word beside it are reworked

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, a British sales tax

indicators.note: prime means foremost, so the first letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A busy garage is irritated at paying tax on top-grade diesel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges the garage into AGGRAE, 'to absorb' takes the tax inside it before the final E, and 'prime' adds the first letter of diesel at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggravated in everyday speech means irritated or exasperated.

clue.text: Coming up, for example, carrying gold snakeshead and yellow flowered shrub

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the other pieces go into the reversed letters
in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
the head of the word snake, its first letter, printed run together as one word

explanation.surface: A plant with yellow blooms, gold and a snake's head among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming up' turns the example abbreviation round in this down clue, giving GE; 'carrying' puts gold and the S of snake inside it. The printed 'snakeshead' is snake's head run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse, also called furze, is a spiny shrub with bright yellow flowers.

clue.text: Dress in wardrobe has a risqué neckline

indicators.note: in means the answer lies within the following words
the neckline sits within the dress, hinting the garment is tucked inside the words

explanation.surface: A garment in the wardrobe has a daringly low neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is a dress of draped cloth worn by women in South Asia.

clue.text: Part of church built as an afterthought to the east

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Part of a church added late on, at its eastern end.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the rounded recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Slowly left the boat

parts.note: the Argo was the boat of Jason and the Argonauts

explanation.surface: Someone slowly left the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a musical direction meaning slowly and broadly.

clue.text: Keeps in order after she failed to finish the coat

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters come behind the shortened word
not finishing means the final letter of the word is dropped
putting in order means rearranging, so the letters of the words beside it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: She keeps things tidy after failing to finish making the coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges KEEPS IN; 'failed to finish' cuts SHE to SH.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepskin is a coat made of the fleece-lined hide of a sheep.

clue.text: Be of the opinion that there is nothing amiss

indicators.note: amiss means wrong, so these letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Believe all is well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amiss' rearranges THERE IS together with O for 'nothing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To theorise is to form a hypothesis or opinion about something.

clue.text: Pointer to what heckler tries to do

definitions.meaning: the indicator on a dial or compass
to provoke or goad a speaker

explanation.definitionFit: A needle is a dial's pointer, and to needle is to provoke or irritate.
